title: Saudi Desert Tree: Focus Stack, HDR Layering, and Light-Bleed Color Grading in Post-Processing

date.display: 2024–2025 (production context from folder name; embedded creation time is 2026 export)

summary: This video is a practitioner-led post-processing walkthrough of a desert-tree landscape shot in a Saudi location, focusing on building depth through a focus-stack HDR workflow, deliberate layer separation, and color/lighting decisions that preserve sky and dune details while isolating a focal tree. The instructor discusses frame selection, composition rules (notably tree placement relative to the horizon), and a suite of techniques to reveal layered depth: auto HDR for layer separation, manual layer painting with a hard-edged brush, dodging and burning to accent the trunk, and subtle light bleeding to guide the viewer’s eye. Color grading centers on color separation via opposite hues, warmth adjustments, and selective color nuance, with additional tips on avoiding artifacts, preserving sky color, and cropping for strong focal points. Throughout, examples emphasize single-tree emphasis, light direction, and the challenge of balancing complex backgrounds with a simple, readable foreground.

sections.title: Frame selection and initial composition
sections.description: The speaker selects frames, notes foreground elements (including a goat in one frame that is discarded), and discusses how different frame parts contribute to the eventual layered depth. Emphasis on choosing a tree and composition that will reveal layers when processed.

sections.title: Focus stack introduction and mid-tone planning
sections.description: Introduction to the focus stack as a key element of the shot. The presenter outlines the expectation that multiple exposure layers will reveal depth, with a plan to extract usable information from mid-tones before deeper processing.

sections.title: HDR-based layer separation and automated workflow
sections.description: The workflow shifts to automatic HDR processing to tease apart layers, followed by discussion of preserving the foreground and the tree while isolating the distant layers. The speaker notes time-saving approaches and the balance between automation and manual refinement.

sections.title: Composition rules and horizon guidance
sections.description: The instructor articulates composition decisions, including the rule about keeping trees completely above or below the horizon and cropping toward a simplistic background to allow the tree to be the focal anchor. The discussion weighs two-tree versus single-tree arrangements and their impact on viewer focus.

sections.title: Targeted local adjustments: trunk emphasis and edge work
sections.description: A sequence of precise, small-area dodges on the trunk and nearby edges is shown to create a stronger three-dimensional read. The presenter stresses careful edge handling to avoid visible seams and to preserve layer separation integrity.

sections.title: Beams creation and light articulation
sections.description: Focus shifts to enhancing light beams and beams-behavior around the sun. The technique includes painting beams with a hard brush at high opacity, refining with a soft brush, and selectively applying auto HDR to brighten or pull beams without over-saturating the sky.

sections.title: Color-grading and color-separation strategies
sections.description: The presenter dives into color separation by hue, using opposite colors (e.g., orange vs blue) to distinguish dunes from sky, and discusses how to modulate warmth and saturation to preserve natural color while emphasizing the scene’s mood.

sections.title: Final polish: sky, clouds, and directional light emphasis
sections.description: The closing section covers final global adjustments to the sky and clouds, additional light bleeding to create a strong focal point, and final cropping decisions. The instructor emphasizes directional light as the key driver of three-dimensionality and mood, and ends with reflections on workflow efficiency and the variability of desert scenes.
